messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — our usage forecast is showing a sharp APAC uplift the week of Nov 21 due to the partner promo. Projection: ~3.2x baseline tokens/sec for JP region at peak.
Julia: where are you pulling the 3.2x from? dashboard link? :eyes:
Sam: from the traffic-sim run I kicked off last night + partner commit numbers. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/capacity/sim-2178 (filtered to jp).
Devon: dug into the sim traces: average prompt length jumps from ~52 to ~118 tokens for that cohort. That changes tokens/sec per request and KV-cache reuse goes down.
Anya: rough ask: what's the 99th pct GPU headroom we need to keep 99.9% latency SLO at 200ms?
Sam: initial, naive calc -> if avg ctx=118 and avg tokens/sec per request ~40, concurrent requests = 4k at peak -> token-rate = 160k tps. With our measured tokens/sec per GPU (non-batched) ~12k tps -> need ~14 GPUs (ceil) for that region — but that's without batching/eviction or network constraints.
Mike: that feels low. Are you accounting for sequence length variance? Also our per-GPU number is for short context; long contexts drop throughput ~30%.
Devon: yes. I re-ran with a long-tail ctx distribution (P95=420). With that, measured tokens/sec per GPU goes to ~8k. Then same traffic -> ~20 GPUs. Also warmup waste for ephemeral models adds ~6% overhead on token counts.
Julia: tradeoffs: can we accept slightly higher latency to cut GPU count? Example: increasing request queuing window to 100ms allows more batching; gig-throughput jumps.
Sam: ran a micro experiment: enabling batching up to 80ms reduced peak GPU need by ~18% in sim (same quality). So latency trade buys capacity.
Anya: what about network egress / rack bandwidth? APAC racks are 10Gb/s — how soon do we hit networking bottlenecks with long sequences?
Devon: good call — with long sequences and larger responses (avg bytes per token ~1.1), we estimate a single rack tops out at ~2.2k tokens/sec for long-chat heavy users. If we place 24 GPUs behind that switch we risk head-of-line. Need to split the serving across two racks or throttle responses.
Sam: procurement note: pre-commit for 2-week extra reserved capacity (40 gpus) in ap-northeast reduces spot/egress frag by a lot, cost delta ~+$28k for the week.
Mike: can we instead shift some traffic to regional fallback (model-quantized variant) that uses half the GPU throughput but trades off 3% quality for 30% lower cost?
Julia: simulation shows fallback + spillover to quantized model reduces peak reserved GPUs by ~35% while keeping error metrics within alerting thresholds for 92% of prompts. But it increases caller-side latency by ~40ms.
Anya: action items: 1) run Monte Carlo with ctx-length volatility (sigma=0.6), 2) include rack-level network saturation in the sim, 3) produce GPU-hours x cost delta CSV for reserve vs spot vs fallback strategies, 4) confirm partner's expected daily session shape.
Devon: I'll add rack egress model and variable ctx distro. Also adding warmup penalty: ephemeral sessions cause avg +0.06 GPU-hours per session.
Sam: timeline: devon/julia can ship updated sim by EOD tomorrow, Anya will try to lock partner session distribution, Mike will provide quality/latency thresholds for quantized fallback.
Infra-bot: reminder: scheduled maintenance in ap-northeast at 03:00 UTC on Nov 19 — it will briefly reduce available GPUs by ~12%.
Mike: flag — if maintenance overlaps promo peak we should schedule blue-green spill or enable more aggressive routing to other regions.
Anya: noted. I'll draft a runbook for promo-week: reserve + fallback + cross-region spill with cost caps.
Sam: thanks team. Please drop final numbers into the shared sheet: `sheets:Capacity/Promo-Nov21` by EOD tomorrow.
Julia: ping me when sim is done — I'll run sensitivity plots (heatmaps of GPU-hours vs latency cap). :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam: cool. closing thread for now, will bump when sims land.
